To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the effect of moisture on colour, texture, and morphology of grain kernels was not significant, and the effect was greater for bulk samples than single kernels.
colour, morphological and textural features extracted from images of individual grain kernels and bulk grain samples were affected by moisture content.
the colour, textural features and kernel morphological features of bulk grain samples and individual grain images were affected to different extents by the grain moisture content.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development and evaluation of digital image processing techniques to extract colour, texture and morphology features of cereal grains.
the development of a machine vision system that can be used in a grading line to determine the moisture content of grain.

the evaluation of the effect of the moisture content on the physical appearance and morphological features of cereal grain kernels and the effect of moisture on grain classification capability using colour, morphology and texture features extracted from images.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
moisture content does affect the physical appearance of grains and the extracted features, however, the effect is not significant enough to be used as an effective classification criterion.
the moisture content of grain has an effect on the colour and morphological features of individual kernels and the colour features of bulk grain.
colour, texture and morphology features of cereal grains are affected by moisture content.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the colour and morphological features are more sensitive to moisture than the textural features.
moisture content had an effect on the physical properties of the grain.
the moisture content of the bulk grain sample had a significant effect on the colour, texture and morphological features extracted from the images.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the colour, texture and morphology of grains are affected by their moisture content.
moisture content of grain has a significant effect on the classification capability using colour, morphology and texture of grain kernels.
colour, textural and morphological features can be used to classify grains at different moisture contents and the effect of moisture on the classification is dependent on the grain type.
